message.content: A cell that contains more than one nucleus is called a **multinucleated cell**. A common example is a **syncytium**, which forms when several individual cells fuse together into a single, large cell with multiple nuclei. Another well‑known type of multinucleated cell is the **osteoclast**, a giant cell involved in bone resorption.
